Only `ha` is then passed on, to `lem_Contra_finiteKR`, `lem_analytic_zero_factor` and `final_ineq1`. I checked the signatures of these three lemmas in the pinned StrongPNT root (`StrongPNT/PNT2_LogDerivative.lean`). All three assume only analyticity on a neighbourhood of the closed unit disk, either as `AnalyticOnNhd` or as the unfolded `∀ z ∈ closedBall 0 1, AnalyticAt`. The target imports `StrongPNT.Erdos970.PNT2_LogDerivative`, but that file is not in the supplied roots. I also looked at the downstream users: `normalized_disk_logDeriv_real_lower_bound`, `normalized_disk_logDeriv_lower_bound` and `normalized_disk_logDeriv_norm_bound`, which in turn are used by the Hecke files. All of them currently pass entire functions. So the generalisation helps future reuse more than it helps the current call sites. Fixing the radii at 1/2, 2/3, 3/4 and 7/8 is a documented, intentional choice ("at the fixed radii needed"), and `final_ineq1` already gives the version with general radii, so I did not report it. `hB : 1 < B` is needed for the `Real.log B` bound to make sense, and `hf0` is used directly. findings.problem: The theorem gives a local estimate on the disk: a bound on the log-derivative for |z| ≤ 1/2, using a bound on |z| ≤ 7/8 and zeros in |z| ≤ 3/4. Yet it requires f to be entire. The proof uses `hf` only to derive `ha : ∀ z ∈ Metric.closedBall (0:ℂ) 1, AnalyticAt ℂ f z`, and every lemma it calls (`lem_Contra_finiteKR`, `lem_analytic_zero_factor`, `final_ineq1`) needs only that weaker, local hypothesis. Requiring global differentiability rules out functions that are analytic near the closed unit disk but have poles or singularities further out. Examples are normalised L-functions with a pole away from the disk, or rational and meromorphic factors. Those are exactly the functions a disk-local zero-free-region argument needs to handle.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the hypothesis with the local one:

theorem normalized_disk_logDeriv (f : ℂ → ℂ)
    (hf : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (Metric.closedBall (0:ℂ) 1)) (hf0 : f 0=1) {B : ℝ} (hB : 1 < B)
    (hb : ∀ z : ℂ, ‖z‖ ≤ (7/8:ℝ) → ‖f z‖ ≤ B) : (same conclusion)

In the proof, drop the `have ha … := fun z _ => hf.analyticAt z` step and use `hf` itself as `ha`. `AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f s` unfolds by definition to `∀ x, x ∈ s → AnalyticAt ℂ f x`, the form the three StrongPNT lemmas take. The rest of the proof is unchanged. Callers that have an entire `f` pass `fun z _ => hf.analyticAt z` (Mathlib's `Differentiable.analyticAt`). Alternatively, keep a thin entire-function corollary with the current statement for the three downstream files. There is no degenerate case: f 0 = 1 still ensures that f is not identically zero on the disk.
findings.benefit: The statement then matches the mathematics it encodes: a purely local Borel–Carathéodory/Jensen-type log-derivative estimate. It can be reused for functions that are holomorphic only near the closed unit disk, without any change to the proof or the constant. It also exposes the true hypothesis expected by the StrongPNT lemmas, so readers can see that global differentiability plays no role.
